caption_used: Distribution of Quantifiers and Operations in Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, and Disjunctive & Conjunctive Reasoning. The Categorical pie chart comprises four segments: Universal Quantifiers (29.07%), Negation (27.91%), Limiter (27.91%), and Existential Quantifiers (15.12%). In the Approximate Number Generation chart, Comparative Relationships constitute the largest share at approximately 48%, followed by Approximate Quantities at 33.26% and Absolute Absence at 18.71%. The Disjunctive & Conjunctive chart shows a near-even split, with Conjunctive slightly dominating at 54.51% over Disjunctive at 45.49%.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The figure presents three pie charts illustrating the distribution of quantifiers and operations across three reasoning categories: Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, and Disjunctive & Conjunctive. The Categorical chart contains four slices: Universal Quantifiers (29.07%, light blue), Negation (27.91%, orange), Limiter (27.91%, light pink), and Existential Quantifiers (15.12%, light green), with no slices exploded or emphasized. The Approximate Number Generation chart has three slices: Approximate Quantities (45.03%, beige), Comparative Relationships (36.26%, light blue), and Absolute Absence (18.71%, lavender), arranged without a clear size-based order. The Disjunctive & Conjunctive chart is divided into two nearly equal halves: Conjunctive (50.49%, light purple) and Disjunctive (49.51%, light blue-gray), with no visual emphasis or explosion. All charts display percentage values directly within each slice and use distinct pastel colors for differentiation; no separate legend is present.
